svg.title: How the M5 judge works and how it was checked before use
svg.text: The LLM judge: how one turn is judged, and how the judge was checked before use
chatbot/judge.py. The same code judges seeded replies and real runs, so the calibration tests exactly the set-up that is used.
Gather the inputs for the turn
- the text of each rule the
Build the packet and the instructions
Packet: the text the judge reads
CONVERSATION SO FAR, THIS TURN (member's message and the reply),
EVIDENCE (what the tools returned), RULES (the spec text),
CORRECT DATES (from code), NOTE, CHECKS TO ANSWER
Ask the judge and read its answer strictly
gpt-6-sol: one call per turn, all the turn's checks at once
The answer must be JSON: pass or fail, and a one-sentence reason, for every check asked.
Not JSON, a check missing or a score instead of pass/fail: asked again once;
still wrong: judge_error, which is never counted as a pass. judge_turn(), parse_verdicts()
Real runs: verdicts saved in judge.json, beside the text checks in checks.json
A turn passes only if every text check and every judge check passes; chatbot.compare reports mean [min-max] over runs.
B. CHECKING THE JUDGE BEFORE TRUSTING IT (IN THIS ORDER)
The judge must get every one right.
No changes for the rest of M5,
